insertions.title: Read the SDI run from command, to error, to control effort
insertions.takeaway: The three aligned plots tell one causal story: command steps create tracking error, the actuator responds, the aircraft output follows with lag and overshoot, and short disturbances perturb the same controlled response.
insertions.asset: screenshots/SimulationDataInspector_Onboarding.jpg, annotated or cropped without fabricating data
plotExplanation: TOP — command steps from 0 to +5 deg at 1 s, to -2 deg at 9 s, and to +3 deg at 15 s; the pitch response follows dynamically rather than instantaneously.
MIDDLE — error = command - response; each command change creates a signed jump, then the error decays and can cross zero when the response overshoots.
BOTTOM — actuator command reacts strongly to error and then relaxes; the retained disturbances are +1.5 deg/s^2 from 7.0 to 7.5 s and -1.0 deg/s^2 from 13.0 to 13.4 s.
INTERPRETATION — this run demonstrates inspectable desktop MIL behavior; use cursors and the CSV for exact values rather than judging only the trace shape.
insertions.notes: Cite scripts/run_training_simulations.m, results/AircraftFeedback_CommandTracking.csv, the SDI screenshot, and the saved SDI view/session. Keep actuator units as documented by the source; do not invent degrees if the signal is dimensionless or unspecified.

insertions.title: Read the 19-case result plot from top to bottom
insertions.takeaway: The top plot proves commanded limiting and fallback behavior, the middle plot proves limiter-active status, and the bottom plot compares numeric error to tolerance; the CSV confirms all numeric, status, timestamp, and timing checks passed.
plotExplanation: TOP — dotted input is clipped to ±18 deg/s only for display; dashed expected and blue actual overlap. Valid Normal-mode commands clamp at ±12, inclusive ±12 stays unclamped, and invalid or disabled cases fall back to zero.

MIDDLE — expected and actual limiter_active overlap. It is true only for valid Normal-mode inputs outside ±12, including the just-outside and large-magnitude cases; it is false at the inclusive boundaries.

BOTTOM — absolute numeric error is plotted on a log axis against the 1e-9 deg/s tolerance. Every retained error is exactly zero, so no positive error trace can appear on the log axis; verify that conclusion in the CSV rather than treating empty space as missing data.
PASS LOGIC — 19/19 requires NumericPass, LimiterActivePass, TimestampPass, and Timing50HzPass for every row, not merely visual overlap.
insertions.notes: Explain that the exact ±1000 deg/s large-magnitude inputs are evaluated even though the display clips them. Cite the test script, result CSV/MAT, and report PNG/HTML. Preserve the timing-tolerance caveat already documented on v6 slide 37.

insertions.title: Open FCS_Data.sldd, then inspect FlightControlBus
insertions.takeaway: The GUI and MATLAB API both lead to the same controlled Design Data entries, and FlightControlBus exposes five named elements whose types, dimensions, units, and descriptions form an explicit interface contract.
insertions.asset: screenshots/FCS_DataDictionary_and_FlightControlBus.png or a new authentic Model Explorer capture if available
accessSteps: GUI — from a linked model, open Model Explorer, follow External Data to data/FCS_Data.sldd, and select Design Data.
MATLAB OPEN — dict = Simulink.data.dictionary.open(fullfile(projectRoot,'data','FCS_Data.sldd')); design = getSection(dict,'Design Data');
BUS ELEMENTS — inspect bus.Elements for q_rate, pitch_angle, mach, air_data_valid, and mode, including units, dimensions, and descriptions.
READABLE INVENTORIES — results/FCS_DataDictionary_Inventory.csv and results/FlightControlBus_Inventory.csv provide retained review views.
insertions.notes: Treat access as read-only teaching unless the learner is authorized to change controlled data. Close the dictionary without inventing changes. Cite the .sldd file, both inventory CSVs, and official MathWorks dictionary and Simulink.Bus documentation.
